Three strip-shaped regions are labeled 1, 2, 3 respectively, and all connect from the upper parallel line to the lower parallel line. The 1st strip is a vertical rectangular strip; the 2nd strip is enclosed by two parallel slanted sides; the 3rd strip is enclosed by two broken-line sides of the same shape, horizontally offset. Reasoning: Let the vertical distance between the two parallel lines be h. For each strip-shaped region, make a horizontal section line at any same height. The horizontal section length of strip 1 is always a; the two slanted sides of strip 2 maintain the same horizontal spacing, so the horizontal section length at any height is also a; the two broken-line sides of strip 3 are horizontal translations of the same shape, therefore the horizontal section length at any height is still a. By Cavalieri's principle, the heights of the three regions are all h, and the length of each horizontal section is all a, so the areas are all equal to ah. Final conclusion: The areas of the three strip-shaped regions are equal.

In strip 1 the cross-section length is a; in strip 2 the two slanted sides remain a horizontal distance apart; in strip 3 the broken side is matched by an identical horizontally shifted broken side, so the cross-section length is still a at every height.
